purpose: Generated implementation reference. Components are separate runtime shapes, not a new API endpoint, combined response envelope, or detection-quality guarantee.
schema_scope: Each component schema is self-contained. Pydantic JSON Schemas describe shape and declared constraints; custom validators and pipeline admission add rules. Only components marked constrained-decoding-schema are sent as response_schema_json.

confidence.meaning: Fixed evidence-tier score, not a calibrated probability of correctness.

candidate_assessment_combination.meaning: Derived provisional status. A refuted HEAD claim or demonstrated unrelated preexisting issue yields refutes. Unknown or refuted broader impact or repair advice leaves a supported local bug uncertain for review; no status removes the original finding. Historical cases retain their original combinations; repair cases show the additional v5 condition for an otherwise supported claim.

ChangedFile.description:
One post-intake file, with status-specific source and rename fields.

Per `DECISIONS.md#020`, added has head only and no deletions; removed
has base only and no additions; modified/renamed have both sources.
Only renamed carries previous_path, and it must differ from path.
intake reads that path from GitHub's previous_filename. The validator
checks these rules for every construction path.
ChangedFile.title: ChangedFile

schema.description:
Immutable metadata and changed-file tuple for one PR review.

Tuple containers prevent mutation that frozen=True alone cannot block.
schema.title: PRContext

ReviewDimension.description: The five review-dimension axes per spec §7.3.
ReviewDimension.title: ReviewDimension

ReviewTier.description:
Per-file review tier produced by the triage node, per spec §4.1.2.

DEEP / STANDARD / SKIM are the LLM-produced classifications; SKIP is
populated by the §6.10 size-cap policy gate (separate spec) when a PR
exceeds the agentic-review thresholds (>1000 changed lines OR >30
files — both PR-level metrics; §6.10 has no per-file size policy).
Lowercase serialized values match project enum convention.
ReviewTier.title: ReviewTier

RiskLevel.description:
PR-level risk classification produced by the triage node, per spec §7.2.

Same ladder shape as FindingSeverity minus INFO (no operational meaning
at PR-level). Distinct from FindingSeverity in scope: RiskLevel measures
the PR as a whole; FindingSeverity measures one finding within it.

Added 2026-05-08 to close the canonical-shape gap. See spec.md §7.2
amendment + specs/2026-05-08-schema-foundation.md for rationale.
RiskLevel.title: RiskLevel

schema.description:
Triage classification plus a captured policy-version anchor.

The four classification fields are required; policy_version defaults to the
active version. The live triage gate rejects a different model-supplied
version. Frozen fields, a copied read-only file map, and canonical dimension
ordering keep checkpoint representations stable.
schema.title: TriageResult

TriageResult.notes: Live responses use numbered file IDs, decoded to the supplied paths before constructing this state record. Policy rejects SKIP, missing/unknown paths and inactive policy versions; reasoning is clamped. Historical records keep path keys.

TriageResponseWire.notes: Example for two files. The actual schema requires file_1 through file_N for the supplied file count; it contains no repository paths. The same count shares a schema. Native validation still checks the returned IDs and policy.

AnalyzeFindingProposalRaw.description:
Model-proposed finding as it arrives in the raw response.

`finding_type` and `evidence_tier` are bounded `str` (NOT the
canonical enums) so a model that returns an off-list value
survives Pydantic construction long enough for the parser to emit
a `FindingProposalRejectedEvent`. Admitted-layer construction is
what enforces enum membership.
AnalyzeFindingProposalRaw.title: AnalyzeFindingProposalRaw

TraceCandidateProposalRaw.description:
Model-proposed trace candidate as it arrives in the raw response.

Parser admits/rejects these alongside their parent finding proposals.

Raw and admitted layers must be materially distinct (not just
default markers), so a downstream variable typed as the raw layer
cannot be silently passed where the admitted layer is expected.
The distinction is in the import field: raw layer carries
`import_string_raw` (the model's claimed import string, unvalidated
bounded string); admitted layer carries `import_string`
(already passed through `coordinates.is_valid_trace_import_string` —
NFC-normalized, per-form shape-checked: absolute/relative Python module or JS/TS
relative-specifier form per `DECISIONS.md#024`, Amended 2026-07-03).
TraceCandidateProposalRaw.title: TraceCandidateProposalRaw

schema.description:
Top-level wrapper around the raw findings array.

Per-call output ceiling at 50 findings — defends against a runaway
model emission that would otherwise saturate the audit stream.
schema.title: AnalyzeResponseRaw

AnalyzeResponseRaw.notes: Bounded raw strings retain unknown categories and tiers for recorded rejection. Schema acceptance does not establish finding admission or evidence validity.

description.description: Non-empty explanation of why this is a problem and what to change, specific to the code under review. Never empty. At most 1000 characters.

evidence.description: Non-empty verbatim quote of the offending line(s) from the code under review. Never empty. At most 2000 characters.

AnalyzeResponseWire.notes: The actual provider schema omits some raw-model bounds and keeps category and tier values as strings. Admission validates canonical values, supplied query IDs, source ranges and evidence separately.

schema.description: Strict envelope for the configured trace model's ordered candidate IDs.
schema.title: TraceRankingResponseRaw

TraceRankingResponseRaw.notes: No response_schema_json is sent. Parser additionally requires exactly the supplied IDs once each; invalid rankings retain the supplied order.

schema.description:
One aggregate trace decision per source_finding_id.

State-layer mirror of `TraceDecisionEvent` (`audit/events.py`).
Frozen + `extra="forbid"` per the cross-boundary schema discipline
in `docs/conventions.md`. Validator-set identical to the audit event
so a producer's construction-time guarantees survive the lift.
schema.title: TraceDecision

CandidateCheckResponseWire.notes: Opt-in investigation output. Citation identity, exact quotes, ranges and source-side requirements are validated after generation. The combined status and suggested severity are derived by code, not returned by the model.

EvidenceTier.description:
How a finding's claim is justified.

OBSERVED: structural — a tree-sitter query in the registry matched
          the location, and the match id is recorded.
INFERRED: structural-by-reference — the agent walked the ast_facts
          trace from a known scope to the claim site, and the
          traversal path is recorded.
JUDGED:   model interpretation only. No structural evidence is
          claimed. Lower confidence by construction.

Values are lowercase per docs/spec.md §7.3, matching the convention
of FindingType and FindingSeverity. The Python member names are
uppercase (PEP 8); only the serialized string values are lowercase.

schema.description:
One finding produced by the agent's review of a PR.

Construction-time validators enforce the proof boundary
(`enforce_proof_boundary` from policy/findings) and the line
constraint (`line_end >= line_start`). Confidence is a computed
field, not a settable attribute.

confidence.description:
Deterministic mapping from evidence_tier per spec §7.3.

OBSERVED=0.9, INFERRED=0.75, JUDGED=0.5. Read-only at the
descriptor level — assigning to `.confidence` raises
AttributeError regardless of model frozen-ness.
confidence.title: Confidence

schema.title: ReviewFinding

ReviewFinding.notes: Serialization includes computed confidence. Policy, proof-boundary, coordinate and identity validators enforce rules beyond the exported JSON Schema.

SummaryText.notes: Nonempty reports use plain model prose, not JSON, with no response schema. Empty reports use the versioned fixed summary without a model call. The completion event identifies the source and hashes raw model or exact template bytes. The final report bounds text. Risk and metrics come from upstream state and code.

PatchSuggestion.description:
One proposed fix, keyed by finding_id, with an exact target-line echo.

Missing/non-UUID IDs and wrong field types reject the batch. Optional fields
allow apply_patch_batch to discard unusable items independently. A null
replacement means no suggested fix (DECISIONS.md#040).

schema.description: The strict envelope for one batched patch-gen response.
schema.title: PatchSuggestionBatch

PatchSuggestionBatch.notes: Separate optional patch call; no response_schema_json is sent. Replacement eligibility, target-line equality and output safety are checked by code.

ReviewMetrics.description:
Per-review statistics computed in synthesize, per spec.md:1106-1114.

All fields derived deterministically from audit_events + analysis_rounds
+ node wall-clock measurement. NOT computed by the LLM call; the
optional summary call produces only summary prose. ge=0 floors match the
LLMCallEvent pricing-field convention (input_tokens, output_tokens,
cost_usd) at audit/events.py:320-323.

schema.description:
Output of the synthesize node, per spec.md:1099-1104.

`findings` is the deduplicated set across all analysis rounds, keyed by
content_hash. The canonical-sort validator enforces deterministic
JSON-payload identity for checkpoint comparison + audit content-hashing:
same logical findings serialize to the same bytes regardless of which
round emitted each instance.

Duplicate content_hash entries are rejected at the schema layer (defense
in depth on top of synthesize's node-side dedup). A producer that
constructs a ReviewReport with two findings sharing a content_hash is
bypassing synthesize's dedup contract — fail-loud here surfaces the bug
rather than silently accepting it.
schema.title: ReviewReport

schema.description:
Agent's gate envelope when it interrupts the graph for HITL approval.

Frozen: the request is the snapshot of the gate context at interrupt time.
A new request is constructed if the gate is re-entered; the old one is
not mutated.
schema.title: HITLRequest

PerFindingDecision.description:
One reviewer's decision on one finding.

Frozen: a per-finding decision is final at construction and cannot be mutated.

Canonical source of HITL override provenance: the `findings`-table override
columns are read-model projections of this (carried on `HITLDecisionEvent`),
never the other way around. See DECISIONS.md#034.
PerFindingDecision.title: PerFindingDecision

PerFindingOutcome.description: Per-finding HITL decision outcomes per spec §7.4.
PerFindingOutcome.title: PerFindingOutcome

schema.description:
Reviewer's full decision set for a HITL gate, final at submission.

Frozen: the submitted decision is final at construction. Per spec §7.4
the field is `decisions: tuple[PerFindingDecision, ...]` (NOT
`per_finding_decisions`; tuple-not-list for true immutability — see
module docstring); the dashboard endpoint constructs this from reviewer
input and the graph resumes with Command(resume=hitl_decision).
schema.title: HITLDecision
